argument:
The bull's matched 18% growth in consolidated revenue and operating income legitimately counters generalising cloud gross-margin pressure into group operating deterioration. Group profitability remains strong. It is not a matched cloud-unit-return measure, however, so the separate evidence of infrastructure and mix reducing cloud gross margin still qualifies the incremental capacity thesis.

Debt and FCF remain unknown; $10.2bn distributions do not establish funded cash generation after investment. OpenAI gains and discrete EPS benefits also need normalisation before using the 29.26x vendor multiple. The clear uptrend favors the bull's business interest, while RSI above 76 and upper-band extension limit fresh entry. Sustained group economics preserve watchlist value but need a per-share cash and price bridge to justify purchase.
key_points: Group operating resilience answers a broad deterioration claim.
Cloud marginal economics and investment-adjusted cash remain unknown.
Normalised valuation and extended entry need support.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull correctly differentiates consolidated operating income from cloud gross margin. It does not answer marginal capacity return, debt or FCF; these remain required to connect strong group results to attractive new-entry value.
